stem: According to the act, what rights did Wyoming women gain?

stimulus.source_note: An Act to Grant to the Women of Wyoming Territory the Right of Suffrage and to Hold Office, approved December 10, 1869. Public domain. Text verified against the American Battlefield Trust transcription (from the Library of Congress) and History of Woman Suffrage, vol. 3.
stimulus.text:
An Act to Grant to the Women of Wyoming Territory the Right of Suffrage and to Hold Office, approved December 10, 1869:

"SECTION 1. That every woman of the age of twenty-one years, residing in this territory, may, at every election to be holden under the laws thereof, cast her vote. And her rights to the elective franchise and to hold office shall be the same under the election laws of the territory, as those of electors."

"SECTION 2. This act shall take effect and be in force from and after its passage."

options.text: The right to own land in the territory, but not to vote
options.misconception: Background: the act is about voting and holding office, not about land ownership.

options.text: The right to vote and to hold office, the same as male electors
The right to serve in the territorial militia only
options.misconception: Background: the act says nothing about the militia; it covers elections and office.

options.text: The right to vote in federal elections only
options.misconception: Background: the act covers 'every election to be holden under the laws thereof,' not federal elections alone.

rationales.A: Background: the act is about voting and holding office, not about land ownership.
rationales.B: Section 1 says it plainly: women may 'cast her vote' at every election, and her rights 'to the elective franchise and to hold office shall be the same ... as those of electors.'
rationales.C: Background: the act says nothing about the militia. It covers elections and office.
rationales.D: Background: the act covers 'every election to be holden under the laws thereof,' not federal elections alone.
rationales.general:
Picture a Wyoming woman walking to the polls in 1870, the first in the nation to vote.
1. Read Section 1 word by word. Every woman of twenty-one may cast her vote.
2. Read the second half. Her rights to vote and to hold office are the same as those of electors.
3. Name the rights. The vote and office-holding, on equal terms.
Remember: a law that says 'the same as' means equal, so read it as equal.
